---
title: "Figures"
---

Figures are essential for visualizing data. Quarto supports **figures generated from R code** as well as **external
images**, with chunk options and Markdown attributes controlling captions, size, and placement.

## Figures Generated from R

**Do:** Run the code below in your own Quarto document. It sets four chunk options:

- `label: fig-scores` — a label enabling this figure to be cross-referenced elsewhere as `@fig-scores`
- `fig-cap` — the figure's caption
- `fig-width` / `fig-height` — the figure's dimensions, in inches

```{r}
#| label: fig-scores
#| fig-cap: "Boxplot of scores by group"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

library(ggplot2)

data <- data.frame(
  Group = c("A", "B", "C"),
  Score = c(5.2, 6.8, 4.9)
)

ggplot(data, aes(x = Group, y = Score, fill = Group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**See:** the resulting figure, with the caption and dimensions from the chunk options applied.

**Predict:** if you add `fig-align: "center"` to this same chunk, what do you expect to change: the figure's content
and size, or something else?

**Explain:** `fig-align` only changes the figure's horizontal placement on the page (left/center/right); the plot
itself, its caption, and its dimensions stay exactly the same. Chunk options that control appearance are independent of
one another, much like the `hist()`/`plot()` styling options covered in the visualization module.

When possible, export figures as vector graphics (PDF or SVG) rather than raster formats (PNG, JPEG): vector graphics
stay crisp at any zoom level or print size, while raster images can look blurry or pixelated when scaled up.

## External Images

Local and web images can also be included, using Markdown's image syntax.

**Local images**, referenced with a project-relative path (leading `/`):

```markdown
![Caption text](/assets/images/ecrins_pano.jpg){#fig-local width=50%}
```

![Caption text](/assets/images/ecrins_pano.jpg){#fig-local width=50%}

**Web images**, linked directly by URL:

```markdown
![Quarto logo](https://quarto.org/quarto.png){width=200px}
```

![Quarto logo](https://quarto.org/quarto.png){width=200px}

Both accept the same `{#fig-label width=...}` attributes as R-generated figures, so they can be sized and
cross-referenced the same way.

::: {.callout-note}
## Common Mistake

A local image path that works on one page can break on another if it's a plain relative path (e.g., `images/photo.jpg`),
since Quarto resolves it relative to that page's own folder — the same class of path problem covered for bibliography
files earlier in this module. For images, a **leading `/`** reliably resolves the path from the project root
regardless of which page includes it, so prefer `/assets/images/photo.jpg` over a bare relative path.
:::

## Referencing Figures in Text

Once a figure has a label, reference it anywhere in the text with `@`:

```markdown
As shown in @fig-scores, group B has the highest score.
```

As shown in @fig-scores, group B has the highest score.

## {{< var tab_title.hint >}}

The plot itself can be built and tested here with `ggplot2`. In an actual `.qmd` file, you would also add these chunk
options above the code to control the label, caption, and size:

```yaml
#| label: fig-mine
#| fig-cap: "Your caption here"
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3
```

## {{< var tab_title.solution >}}

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

data <- data.frame(
  Group = c("A", "B", "C"),
  Score = c(5.2, 6.8, 4.9)
)

ggplot(data, aes(x = Group, y = Score, fill = Group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_minimal()
```

In a real `.qmd` file, this chunk would also carry `#| label: fig-mine`, `#| fig-cap: "Your caption here"`,
`#| fig-width: 5`, and `#| fig-height: 3` as chunk options above the code.
